name: OpSystem Core
fullName: OpSystem Core — evidence store, jobs, search and analysis backend
summary: The Go backend the OpSystem desktop and Android apps connect to. It stores incidents and hash-verified evidence, runs background jobs, indexes OSINT documents and posts for search, produces AI-assisted reports, streams live events and backs itself up. These guides are for operators and integrators working with its HTTP API.
gettingAccess: Every /api/ route needs a bearer token: either a device token issued when an operator signs in or enrols, or one of the static API keys the core's administrator configures for scripts and collectors. A super user is created at the core's first start and its one-time password is written only to the core's own data directory, for the estate operator to retrieve. Keys and tokens are never published in this academy; ask the core's administrator for yours.

guides.title: Authenticate a client
guides.goal: Obtain a device token (or use a static key) and send it correctly on every request.
before: An operator account or a one-time enrolment code, or a static API key from the administrator.
steps: Check the core is up: GET /healthz needs no token and answers status ok (or 503 degraded with a reason).
As an operator, POST /api/v1/auth/login with JSON {email, password, device_label}. The response carries a long-lived device token; store it on the device.
Or exchange an enrolment code: POST /api/v1/auth/enrol with {code, device_label}. Codes are single-use and valid for 24 hours.
Send the token on every /api/ request as the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. For EventSource, which cannot set headers, pass it as ?token=.
Confirm who you are with GET /api/v1/auth/me.
When a device is retired, POST /api/v1/auth/logout to revoke its own token.
guides.result: Requests succeed and anything you create is stamped with the signed-in operator's LO number. Static keys work too, but carry no identity.

troubleshooting.fix: The header is missing, malformed or the token was revoked. Sign in or enrol again.

troubleshooting.problem: Login or enrol answers with a rate-limit error
troubleshooting.fix: Both routes are rate-limited. Wait before retrying.

guides.title: Create an incident and upload hash-verified evidence
guides.goal: Open an incident and store a file or text exhibit so the core can confirm it holds the exact bytes captured in the field.
steps: POST /api/v1/incidents with JSON including title (required) and optionally callsign, location_name, geofence_lat, geofence_lng, geofence_radius_km, keywords, threat_level and summary. Status defaults to ACTIVE_DISPATCH and threat_level to MEDIUM.
Compute the SHA-256 of the exhibit on the capturing device before upload.

POST /api/v1/evidence as multipart/form-data with incident_id and evidence_type (both required; types include IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, POST, SPECTRUM, GSM_LOG, DOCUMENT), and source, title, origin, recorded_by_lo, client_sha256, optional captured_at (RFC 3339) and metadata (a JSON object).
Attach the bytes as the file field, or send text_content instead for text-only exhibits such as posts or GSM logs.
Read the response item: hash_verified is true only when the server's hash equals your client_sha256.

List an incident's evidence with GET /api/v1/evidence?incident=<id>; fetch bytes with GET /api/v1/evidence/<id>/file (the X-Evidence-SHA256 header carries the hash) and an image thumbnail with /thumbnail.
Close an incident with POST /api/v1/incidents/<id>/close, or mark it inactive with POST /api/v1/incidents/<id>/inactive.
guides.result: The evidence is stored once per unique hash, has a chain-of-custody entry, is categorised and indexed, and an evidence.captured event is published. IMAGE uploads queue a thumbnail job.

troubleshooting.fix: The bytes received differ from what the device sealed, or client_sha256 was not sent. Re-upload from the local sealed copy and compare hashes.

troubleshooting.problem: 400 either a file or text_content is required
troubleshooting.fix: Send a file field or a non-empty text_content.
The incident_id does not exist; create the incident first.

guides.title: Search everything the core holds
guides.goal: Run full-text searches across incidents, evidence text, OSINT documents, posts and reports.
steps: Call GET /api/v1/search?q=<words>. Add &limit=<n> to change the number of hits (default 50).
End a term with * to prefix-match it (for example grayston*).
Read each hit's kind, id, title, snippet and score, and follow the id to the matching resource.
guides.result: A ranked list of hits from the in-memory index, which is rebuilt from the stored data at every start.

troubleshooting.problem: A just-fetched page is not found
troubleshooting.fix: OSINT pages are indexed when their osint.fetch job finishes. Check the job's status first.

guides.title: Run background jobs and collect OSINT pages
guides.goal: Fetch a public page into an incident and follow jobs to completion.
before: An authenticated client and an incident ID.
steps: To collect a page, POST /api/v1/osint/fetch with {url, incident_id}. The core fetches the page, strips it to text, categorises and indexes it.

Other work goes through POST /api/v1/jobs with {type, params}. The accepted types are osint.fetch (url, incident_id), evidence.thumbnail (evidence_id), evidence.categorise (evidence_id) and osint.categorise (document_id).
Follow progress with GET /api/v1/jobs, optionally ?status=queued, running, done or failed, or GET /api/v1/jobs/<id>.
List collected pages with GET /api/v1/osint/documents and read one with /api/v1/osint/documents/<id>.
guides.result: The job moves from queued to running to done (or failed with a reason). Jobs are persisted and re-queued after a restart.

troubleshooting.fix: The core refuses targets whose host is written as localhost, a loopback, link-local, 10.x or 192.168.x address, or the all-zeros address. It checks only the host as written and does not cover the 172.16–172.31 private range, so do not rely on it to keep internal addresses out; use a public address.
The type is not one of the four accepted job types.

guides.title: Push social posts from a collector and subscribe to live events
guides.goal: Feed posts into an incident and react to changes as they happen.
before: A static API key or device token.
steps: POST /api/v1/social/ingest with {"posts": [ ... ]}. Each post needs incident_id and text; author, platform, views, verified, threat_score, timestamp, matched_keywords, source_url and similar fields are optional.
Read the response count ingested; posts missing incident_id or text are skipped. The core creates no posts of its own.
Read posts for an incident with GET /api/v1/social?incident=<id>.
Open GET /api/v1/events as a Server-Sent Events stream (token as ?token= for EventSource).
Handle the event types incident.updated, evidence.captured, evidence.updated, job.*, osint.indexed, report.created and social.ingested.
guides.result: Ingested posts appear in the apps' social stream for that incident, and connected clients refresh when events arrive.

troubleshooting.fix: Every post lacked incident_id or text. Add both.

guides.title: Export an incident dossier and run AI analysis
guides.goal: Get everything held on an incident and produce cited AI reports from it.
before: An AI provider key configured on the core by its administrator.
steps: GET /api/v1/incidents/<id>/dossier for the dossier as JSON (record, evidence with text and hashes, OSINT documents in full, posts, timeline, category counts), or add ?format=text for the plain-text export.
POST /api/v1/analysis with {incident_id, task, question, lo_number}. task is one of sitrep, action_plan, timeline, entities, osint_leads or ask; question is used with ask.
List reports with GET /api/v1/reports and read one with GET /api/v1/reports/<id>. A report.created event is published for each.
guides.result: A stored report that cites evidence IDs and separates what is verified from what is reported.

troubleshooting.fix: No AI provider key is set on the core. The core never produces a placeholder report; ask the administrator to configure one.

guides.title: Manage operators and devices
guides.goal: Invite operators, reset passwords, disable accounts and revoke lost devices.
before: A device token belonging to a SUPER_USER operator.
steps: POST /api/v1/operators/invite with {email, name, role, lo_number}. Roles are SUPER_USER, ANALYST and OFFICER. The response carries a one-time code; the apps wrap it into an enrolment link.
List operators with GET /api/v1/operators.
Set a password for someone with POST /api/v1/operators/<id>/password.
Disable or re-enable an operator with POST /api/v1/operators/<id>/disabled.
Revoke a single device with POST /api/v1/devices/<id>/revoke (the device's owner may also do this).
guides.result: The team list reflects the change; a disabled operator's devices stop working.

troubleshooting.fix: These routes need a SUPER_USER device token; static API keys carry no identity and cannot use them.

troubleshooting.problem: A self-service password change is refused
troubleshooting.fix: Where the access lock is switched on (UAT), operators cannot change their own passwords; a super user may still set one.

guides.title: Back up, copy off and restore the core's data
guides.goal: Make sure a verified backup exists, keep a copy on another machine, and restore from it.
before: A bearer token or static API key accepted by the core (the backup routes need authentication but no particular role).
Access to the machine running the core for restores.
steps: Check freshness: GET /healthz includes backup.stale, and after ten minutes of uptime it answers 503 if no verified archive is younger than 48 hours.
Nightly backups run by themselves at the configured hour (default 23:45 UTC). To take one now, POST /api/v1/backups, or run ./start.sh backup [stage] on the machine.
List archives with GET /api/v1/backups.

From another machine, on a schedule, run scripts/fetch-backup.sh <core-url> <bearer-key> [dest-dir]; add --snapshot to pull a live archive instead of the latest nightly. The script checks the downloaded archive with tar before keeping it.

To restore, run ./start.sh restore <archive.tar.gz> [stage], which stops the service, restores and starts it again; or run opsystemcore -restore <archive> (add -force only to overwrite a non-empty data directory).
guides.result: Every kept archive has been read back in full; archives are retained for 14 days, and a restore reproduces the data and evidence files.

troubleshooting.problem: fetch-backup.sh says no backup on the core yet
troubleshooting.fix: Take one with POST /api/v1/backups or ./start.sh backup, then fetch again.
The data directory is not empty, or the archive failed verification. Check the archive; use -force only when you mean to overwrite.

troubleshooting.problem: The core will not start in a deployed stage
troubleshooting.fix: It refuses to start without its separate backup volume and without API keys configured.
